section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining how conversations about weight loss/dieting versus exercise differentially predict body appreciation among undergraduate women. The study supported hypotheses that exercise conversations predict increased body appreciation while weight loss/diet conversations predict decreased appreciation, with these relationships mediated by body-as-object versus body-as-process orientations. The authors acknowledge three main limitations: the sample comprised only undergraduate women limiting generalizability, measures of body image and body orientation could be refined, and the cross-sectional design prevents determination of causal direction.
